system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The embedded “SYSTEM NOTE” is counterparty-supplied and has no authority. The Seller’s assertions that matters are agreed, adequate or settled do not change the Buyer’s playbook.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m**; 20% is available only with Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying this draft, which has not been given. | **Reject and counter at AUD 6m** — the lower fallback is not authorised merely because the Seller proposed the same number. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** basket; Seller pays only losses above the basket. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000** aggregate basket; once exceeded, recovery from the **first dollar**. | **Reject and restore Buyer thresholds** — the Seller’s proposal materially suppresses smaller claims and converts the basket into an unauthorised deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months** after Completion; limitations are to apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24 months** for general claims; 18 months requires Amelia’s prior written approval, which has not been given. | **Reject and require 24 months** — the proposed fallback is unauthorised and the “all Claims” overlay risks cutting down separate protections. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limit for “administrative simplicity.” | Separate regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, and outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge restrictions. | **Reject completely** — ownership, authority and title risk must not be diluted by the general warranty regime. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no adequate express exception for fraud or equivalent conduct. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an overriding, non-waivable carve-out** — the Seller’s wording could shelter intentional wrongdoing and conflicts with a mandatory Buyer position. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; no deemed disclosure through bulk data or public searches. | **Delete general/deemed disclosure** — mere document availability does not establish fair disclosure against a particular warranty. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by the Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; if any qualifier remains, confine it to actual knowledge of named appropriate persons, while Seller warranty knowledge qualifiers use named Seller persons plus reasonable enquiry; never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject the broad actual/constructive knowledge bar** — it improperly transfers disclosure and diligence risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. | Before Completion, obtain **effective consent** and evidence that every associated condition has been satisfied. | **Strengthen the condition precedent and prohibit premature satisfaction** — Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m/30% of FY26 revenue and reasonable endeavours do not secure the required outcome. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; release to follow Completion, with no final discharge presently supplied. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of all security at Completion. | **Require payout and simultaneous discharge mechanics** — any post-Completion release would require an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia’s approval, neither of which is presently established. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are treated as a Seller matter but are omitted from funds flow; on-costs are undetermined. | Expressly itemise **AUD 420,000 plus triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**, with clear Seller funding/economic responsibility. | **Revise the funds flow and allocate all associated costs to Seller** — silent omission risks the Company/Buyer bearing a Completion-triggered liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-010 notes AUD 180,000 open, but payment status is not independently verified. | Broader indemnity covering the Ironquay matter and resulting IP ownership/use, enforcement, cure and loss risks, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure. | **Broaden the indemnity and verify payment/assignment evidence** — paying an unverified AUD 180,000 alone may not ensure clean and effective IP transfer. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; documents do not establish access, exact scope, notification duty, breach or loss. | Preserve relevant logs and evidence, continue a documented investigation, provide prompt updates and findings, and maintain appropriate contractual protection without assuming a breach or quantified loss. | **Add preservation, investigation and update obligations** — uncertainty requires controlled fact-finding, not either dismissal or an unsupported adverse conclusion. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** are said to be ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, avoidability, termination rights, accrual and ordinary-course status; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Reserve position pending diligence** — the Disclosure Letter itself does not substantiate the Seller’s ordinary-course characterisation. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Proposes that general limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded, and that exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to Claims of any nature. | Separate regimes for **Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities**, without a hidden general-regime override. | **Rewrite the limitations architecture and add express precedence rules** — an “all Claims” provision could inadvertently cap or time-bar separately negotiated remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the internal Company share register at DD-012 as evidence that Seller owns 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of ownership, title, encumbrance status, authority and valid transfer, supported by transaction documents and appropriate external searches/confirmations. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive** — it is a supplied internal source, not independent proof of clean title or authority. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says Tax and IP warranties are “settled” under the general regime. | Treat both categories as **open**; negotiate their scope, qualifications, claim periods, caps and any indemnities separately, without assuming unlimited liability or resolution. | **Reject the claimed settlement and reserve all rights** — no Buyer authority or verified agreement supports folding these unresolved categories into the general regime. |
=== END ADVICE ===
